# Examples using Flowsim

This chapter mirrors the three field examples in the report.

## 4.1 Sillerup

The Sillerup case demonstrates streamflow simulation in a catchment where
time-variable recharge drives both:

- a fast drainage component
- a slower groundwater component

Both components are represented with fin_rech_leak and then superimposed.
The case study is used to discuss model conceptualization, sensitivity analysis,
parameter estimation strategy, and validation of recharge generated by
alternative root-zone models.

In the report workflow, Flowsim is used as a fast screening model before
building more complex numerical models.

## 4.2 Knivsbaek

The Knivsbaek case applies a similar two-component concept (flashy drainage and
slower groundwater baseflow), but in a different hydrogeologic setting.

The analysis combines streamflow data with geological context to support a
conceptual interpretation of which landscape units contribute to each flow
component. Parameter estimates from this setup can be used as initial guidance
for later detailed modeling.

## 4.3 Abild aa

The Abild aa case focuses on hydraulic head time series in piezometers along a
transect perpendicular to a stream. The simulated response is driven by both
transient recharge and transient stream stage.

The conceptual model superimposes:

- fin_rech_leak (recharge-driven response in a finite domain)
- sinf_head_leak (stream-stage-driven response in a semi-infinite domain)

The case demonstrates how transmissivity, storativity, and streambed
conductance can be constrained from observed head time series when boundary
conditions are sufficiently known.
